Complete Empirical Research Plan  

-------------------------------------------------  

1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Fuzzy Regression-Discontinuity Design (RDD) at the proposal-meeting level, supplemented with staggered DID/event-study panels for post-meeting dynamics.

Why RDD is appropriate  
• Running variable = percentage of votes cast FOR the proposal (continuous 0–100).  
• Cutoff = simple majority (50 %).  
• Institutional facts: (i) no managerial ability to withdraw proposals, (ii) investors learn outcomes only at the meeting, (iii) distribution of vote shares is smooth around 50 %.  
• Because proposals are advisory, “pass” induces a large but incomplete jump in the probability of subsequent implementation (31 % → 3 %); hence a fuzzy RD gives a local‐average causal effect of IMPLEMENTATION on outcomes.  
• Short-run stock-price reactions can also be estimated with a sharp RD because the market reacts to PASS (discrete news).  
• Long-run outcomes (acquisitions, CAPEX, Tobin’s Q, etc.) are analyzed in a two-stage least squares RD panel: PASS (instrument) → IMPLEMENTATION → outcome.

2. Treatment and Control  
Treatment variable  
Tᵢ = 1 if proposal passes the 50 % threshold (vote_share ≥ 0.5). For IV estimates the endogenous regressor is Implementationᵢ (indicator that the firm actually changes the governance feature within 18 months after the meeting).  

Control group  
Observations with vote_share just below 50 %. Counterfactual = what would have happened had a firm that almost passed instead failed.  

Timing / event date  
t = 0: annual-meeting date.  
• Short-run: cumulative abnormal return (CAR_{–1,+1}).  
• Medium-run: CAR_{+2,+90}.  
• Long-run firm variables: fiscal year t + 1 and t + 2.  

Running variable & cutoff  
Xᵢ = vote_shareᵢ − 0.50, cutoff at 0.  
Bandwidths chosen by Calonico-Cattaneo-Titiunik MSE-optimal and ±5 p.p. as robustness.  

3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
A1. Continuity: Potential outcomes and covariates evolve smoothly in vote share absent treatment.  
 Plausible: proposal withdrawal impossible; shareholders cannot micro-target vote total.  

A2. No precise manipulation of vote share at 50 %.  
 Plausible: open-market ballots, dispersed voters. Testable via McCrary density.  

A3. First-stage relevance: Passing materially increases implementation probability.  
 Empirically strong (Δ ≈ 28 p.p.).  

A4. Exclusion (for IV): Passage affects outcomes only through implementation, not via other simultaneous shocks exactly at 50 %.  
 Plausible because PASS is the only discrete jump; we will probe with multiple proposals and covariate checks.  

A5. Stable Unit Treatment (no cross-proposal spillovers within a meeting over ±2 p.p. bandwidth).  
 Potentially mild concern; clustering and multiple-proposal controls mitigate.

4. Threats to Identification & Remedies  
Threat 1: Sorting/manipulation of vote totals.  
 • McCrary density check; “donut” RD dropping votes in (–0.5, +0.5 p.p.).  

Threat 2: Anticipation—market could partially price passage probability pre-meeting.  
 • Use narrow window CAR_{–1,+1}.  
 • Show flat pre-trend returns CAR_{–30,–2} with RD.  

Threat 3: Multiple proposals in same meeting create correlated shocks.  
 • Include meeting-level fixed effects when several proposals fall within bandwidth.  
 • Alternative sample restricted to meetings with a single close-call proposal.

5. R Code Outline  

```r
# 0. Packages
library(data.table); library(fixest); library(rdrobust); library(sandwich); library(lmtest)

# 1. Load data
prop  <- fread("riskmetrics_proposals.csv")      # one row per proposal
prices<- fread("crsp_prices.csv")                # daily returns
comp  <- fread("compustat_fundamentals.csv")
gind  <- fread("gindex.csv")

# 2. Merge and variable construction
prop[, pass := as.integer(vote_share >= 0.50)]
prop[, running := vote_share - 0.50]
prop[, meeting_id := paste0(firm_id,"_",year(meeting_date))]

# implementation within 18 months
prop[, implement := as.integer(implemented_date <= meeting_date + 548)]   # 18*30.4 days

# outcome 1: CAR[-1,1]
# (Assume abnormal returns already merged in `prices`)
car <- prices[, .(CAR = sum(abret)), by = proposal_id]
prop <- merge(prop, car, by = "proposal_id", all.x = TRUE)

# 3. Fuzzy RD: Implementation first stage
bw <- rdbwselect(y = prop$implement, x = prop$running)$bws[1]   # optimal bandwidth

rd1 <- rdrobust(y = prop$implement, x = prop$running, fuzzy = NULL,
                c = 0, h = bw, kernel = "triangular")

# 4. Second stage: Impact on CAR
rd2 <- rdrobust(y = prop$CAR, x = prop$running, fuzzy = prop$pass,
                c = 0, h = bw, kernel = "triangular")

# 5. Panel RD for long-run outcomes (year t+1)
panel <- merge(prop, comp, by = c("firm_id","fyear"), all.x = TRUE)
panel[, post := (fyear >= year(meeting_date) + 1)]

iv_rd <- feols(TobinQ ~ 1 | implement ~ pass, data = panel[abs(running) <= 0.05],
               cluster = "firm_id")

# 6. Robustness: Alternate bandwidth 3%
rd2_rb <- rdrobust(y = prop$CAR, x = prop$running, fuzzy = prop$pass,
                   c = 0, h = 0.03, kernel = "triangular")
```

6. Expected Results  
• Immediate CAR: +1 % to +1.5 % for close-call passes (≈ 0.25 σ of daily stock returns).  
• Long-run:  
 – Tobin’s Q +0.05 to +0.10 (≈ 3–5 % of one std. dev.).  
 – Acquisitions count –10 % (fewer empire-building deals).  
 – CAPEX/R&D mix: lower CAPEX, higher R&D for tech-intensive firms.  
Magnitude guided by prior literature on antitakeover provision removals and board independence.

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (1 = clear, 0 = questionable)  
C1: No manipulation of running variable …… 1  
C2: Covariate continuity at cutoff ………… 1  
C3: First-stage relevance (fuzzy RD) ……… 1  
C4: Exclusion restriction (pass → outcome only via implement) … 0.5  
C5: Robustness to bandwidth/kernels ……… 1  

Total = 4.5 / 5.
